transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start time: 2026-09-14T15:00:00Z
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Marina Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE - brief), Claire Zhou (Redwood Partner Ops), Priya Nair (Solaris Head of Partnerships), Danielle Wu (Solaris Cloud Architect), Miguel Santos (Solaris Product), Ibrahim al-Hassan (Solaris Security)
Links shared: packaging checklist draft - https://redwood.com/partners/solarispkg (draft), sample helm chart repo - https://git.redwood.example/solarischarts, pilot infra spreadsheet - https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/solarispilot

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Kickoff: packaging & listing steps, infra access and security artifacts needed, timeline. 

[00:00] Marina: Alright, good afternoon everybody, thanks for taking the time. I'm Marina, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood, and with me is Ethan who will drive the helm/chart and infra stuff. Um, Samir will drop in for the compliance bit. How's everyone doing at Solaris?

[00:18] Priya: Hi Marina, hey team, thanks. We're excited. Quick intros — Danielle is our cloud architect, Miguel product, Ibrahim our security lead. We're aiming to get on the AWS marketplace and want to make sure the ref arch and the listing packaging meet the marketplace and Redwood requirements.

[00:35] Marina: Great. Goal for today is to walk through the packaging checklist, required artifacts, the reference architecture for customers who want private deployments via VPC, and to agree on next steps, timeline for a pilot. I'll start with the checklist.

[00:50] Ethan: Uh yeah I'll try to keep it technical, and then I can follow up with a validation run. Quick note: Redwood has slight variances between Hosted API listing versus Dedicated/Private images — sometimes the doc calls it Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Dedicated but the packaging differs.

[01:10] Danielle: Can you clarify that? Are you saying the same container is used for both hosted and dedicated? We anticipate needing a different image for customers who want to run in their VPC.

[01:23] Ethan: Good question. For AWS listing, typically you provide a container image (ECR) plus a helm chart for customer deployment. For hosted we route to Redwood's hosted endpoints; for Dedicated/Private, we provide an image and helm that customers deploy into their VPC/cluster. There are config flags for KMS key integration and telemetry — we can show the sample values file.

[01:45] Priya: Where does the marketplace listing point to for the private option? I'm trying to understand the UX — does the marketplace spin up the cluster or just provide links?

[01:55] Marina: Marketplace is primarily a procurement listing: it provisions a contract and can trigger an automation to pull from ECR and install but typically the customer or their infra team completes the deployment. For AWS SaaS integration there's also a SaaS-based listing but given Solaris wants on-prem-like VPC deployments, we'll use the Bring-Your-Own-Infrastructure path. The listing will include deployment instructions and a pointer to the helm chart repo.

[02:20] Miguel: So we're looking at two paths: 1) 'Quickstart' hosted connect where customers consent and data routes to Redwood Hosted API, and 2) 'Self-hosted' where they deploy our container into their cluster and manage keys. We want to surface both.

[02:36] Marina: Yep, that's typical. Important to call out the security artifacts we need for the listing: SOC2 summary, data residency statements, KMS/HSM approach, audit log retention — Ibrahim, can you speak to our current posture?

[02:50] Ibrahim: Sure. We're SOC2 Type II in progress, we have a lot of controls in place but the certificate is expected in Q4. I can export the control matrix and a summary with the dates. Also we use AWS KMS, CMKs, and we can provide architecture diagram for key usage and any cross-account roles for ECR pull.

[03:10] Marina: Perfect. That will be fine for the listing; we'll note 'SOC2 pending - control matrix provided'. Marketplaces rarely block for that if you provide a timeline.

[03:23] Samir (joins): Hey all, sorry for the delay. Quick compliance note: AWS Marketplace sometimes asks for a dispatchable contact and a vulnerability disclosure program link; also check the export controls doc.

[03:40] Danielle: Thanks. On the technical side, what's the recommended network topology for private customers? We want to include a reference arch in the listing that covers VPC peering versus VPC endpoints.

[03:52] Ethan: For low-latency and secure setups, we recommend the following: customer's VPC runs the app pods, we recommend either a VPC endpoint pattern for control plane integrations or Cross-account roles with limited IAM to pull images from ECR. For NVidia GPUs or specialized inference, you'd use Dedicated pools — in the marketplace listing we'll provide both a basic K8s pattern and a higher performance pattern that references Redwood's 'Dedicated' offering. Note: sometimes the transcript generator appends 'Redwood Ded... Dedi-cate' which is the Dedicated product.

[04:30] Miguel: Can we include a diagram that shows where KV cache and prefix caching sits? Customers often ask how to integrate the KV cache with our stateful services.

[04:40] Ethan: Yes, include a component: 1) Application layer (Solaris service) 2) Redwood model inference contraints (KV cache optional) 3) optional caching layer like Redis to store prefix and session state. We'll provide a sample manifests folder in the helm chart for enabling/disabling KV caching.

[05:05] Priya: Are there any hard constraints from AWS Marketplace about container size or runtime? We have a couple of large images due to language models & tokenizers.

[05:15] Marina: AWS doesn't enforce a strict size limit for ECR images, but large images can slow onboarding and pull times for customers. Best practice is to keep the runtime slim and have model artifacts downloaded at runtime or hosted separately. For Redwood Dedicated deployments we often recommend quantized models to reduce image + memory.

[05:37] Danielle: That makes sense — we can change our Docker layering to keep the core runtime < 2GB and fetch model blobs from S3. Does Redwood support S3 pulls on first start?

[05:48] Ethan: Yes. We'll include a sample initContainer in the helm chart that fetches model blobs from the customer's S3 bucket using an assumed role. We'll document required IAM permissions.

[06:15] Marina: Quick pause — I've posted a draft packaging checklist link in the chat: https://redwood.com/partners/solarispkg this is a living doc. We'll run through the top-level items now.

[06:30] (reads from checklist) Marina: Items: 1) ECR repo & image URI; 2) Helm chart with values schema; 3) sample values.yaml incl KMS key id and telemetry toggles; 4) Reference arch diagram for VPC deployments; 5) Security artifacts (SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit description, SSO/SAML options); 6) Support contact and escalation path; 7) Pricing tiers & metering hooks.

[07:05] Priya: On pricing: our product team will likely want metered usage. How does Redwood expect metering data for marketplace billing?

[07:16] Marina: For SaaS we integrate with billing hooks; for self-hosted deployments, marketplace handles procurement and then you invoice as per your agreement or you can use metering agents. We can talk about metering patterns in a follow-up. For the pilot let's keep it simple — fixed monthly seat or instance-based billing.

[07:40] Miguel: Will there be a Redwood SDK or agent inside the container for telemetry? We try to avoid outbound telemetry to third parties in self-hosted installs.

[07:50] Ethan: We provide an optional telemetry shim that can send usage events to Redwood if customers opt into SaaS reporting. For privacy-first customers, the shim can be disabled and logs kept locally or forwarded to customer's ELK/observability stack. We'll highlight that in the values.yaml.

[08:10] Danielle: Can we see the sample values file?

[08:15] Ethan: I'll show the gist quickly. (screen share described) values.yaml: replicaCount, image.repository, image.tag, model.fetch.s3.enabled, kms.keyArn, telemetry.enabled: false, telemetry.endpoint: '', storage.persistence.size, resources.requests/limits. We have comments inline.

[08:48] Priya: Regarding auth: for enterprise customers who need SSO, does Redwood support SAML/SSO integrations? We need to list supported methods.

[08:58] Marina: Yes SAML and OIDC are supported, plus token-based API keys for service-to-service. For the marketplace listing include a section: "Authentication options: SSO (SAML/OIDC), API tokens, and mTLS optional".

[09:18] Ibrahim: For the security slide — we will supply the KMS architecture and cross-account role. Are there any requirements re: HSM? Some customers request HSM-backed keys.

[09:28] Ethan: We can document both; if a customer demands HSM, they'll need to bring that into their account. For Dedicated deployments there's a pattern to integrate with cloud provider HSMs or bring-your-own key material. We'll add a note.

[09:46] Samir: Also note that if Solaris plans to collect logs that contain PII you should document the retention and redaction approach for the marketplace listing.

[09:56] Miguel: Good call. We'll add a column in the pilot spreadsheet for PII handling.

[10:05] Marina: Moving on to packaging specifics — AWS listing requires a product short description, images/screenshots, a support contact, and a minimum of the architecture doc. We recommend a 'quickstart' sample that can be executed in 10-15 minutes for trial customers. Does Solaris have a quickstart script?

[10:24] Priya: We have a terraform repo that can spin up a dev cluster and deploy a tiny model. We can adapt that to a quickstart. Danielle, can you point to the repo?

[10:33] Danielle: Yes, it's at https://git.solaris.example/dev-quickstart. We'll add a lightweight manifest for the marketplace quickstart.

[10:40] Ethan: Perfect. For the helm chart we'll add a flag to enable the quickstart which uses a small fake model so image size is tiny.

[11:00] Marina: Timeline? If we get the basic artifacts by Sept 21, Redwood can validate and request any minor changes; target pilot listing mid-October. Does that timeline work?

[11:12] Priya: Yes that sounds reasonable. We have internal approvals the week of Sept 20.

[11:20] Danielle: One more technical Q: For customers who want Redwood-managed model updates, what's the process? Does the marketplace listing need to call out auto-updates?

[11:31] Marina: If you offer auto-updates, you need to document the update channel and provide a rollback plan. Many enterprise customers prefer manual control. We'll recommend default off for auto-updates and document how to enable it.

[11:45] (long silence/typing)

[12:10] Miguel: On the reference arch doc, can Redwood provide a templated diagram we can adapt?

[12:20] Marina: Yes, we have a reference arch template — I'll attach after the call. Link: https://redwood.com/partners/refarch-template.

[12:35] Ibrahim: Regarding audit logs — does Redwood expect logs to be shipped to Redwood's account for Dedicated customers? Or kept local and only metadata reported?

[12:45] Ethan: By default, logs stay local. For Hosted API logs are in Redwood's observability. For Dedicated/private, logs are customer-managed. If you want Redwood Support access, we can enable a cross-account read-only role and define S3/CloudWatch buckets with restricted access.

[13:10] Priya: OK that works. Next, packaging for the marketplace sometimes requires a security questionnaire. Do you have an example?

[13:20] Samir: Yes, AWS security questionnaire is usually a few pages. We'll drop a redacted sample. Also include an export controls checklist.

[13:30] Danielle: Can we go over the helm values for KMS integration?

[13:36] Ethan: Sure, example snippet: security.kms.enabled: true, security.kms.keyArn: arn:aws:kms:..., security.kms.roleToAssume: arn:aws:iam::..., encryption.atRest: true. We'll also provide a sample policy for the cross-account role.

[14:05] Miguel: For observability, we need to show latency SLOs customers can expect when running in-cloud versus on-prem. Do you have sample numbers?

[14:16] Marina: We have benchmarks in our performance pack. Typical median token latency for a 2k sequence on x86 GPU is X ms (placeholder) and when using quantized models it drops. We'll give recommended SLO strings to include — for example: p50 < 200ms (small model), p95 < 600ms (varies).

[14:38] Miguel: Please make sure those are marked as estimate since customers will have different infra.

[14:45] Marina: Absolutely. We'll label them as 'example bench results from Redwood internal testing'.

[15:00] Priya: Any blockers we should be aware of?

[15:05] Danielle: We need clarity on image signing and verification. Some enterprise customers insist on signed images and SBOMs.

[15:12] Ethan: We support image signing and can provide SBOM generation steps. We'll add a CI snippet to produce SBOMs and sign images with Sigstore or cosign.

[15:30] Priya: About listing metadata — do we need a legal agreement or can we handle procurement through AWS Marketplace contract?

[15:40] Marina: You can do procurement through AWS Marketplace, but Redwood recommends having a master services agreement for Dedicated/Private customers. For marketplace purchases it's common to have a post-procurement activation step where you sign the PSU or MSA. We'll draft suggested language.

[16:05] (notes, links posted in chat) Marina: Posting the sample helm repo: https://git.redwood.example/solarischarts (read-only). Also packaging checklist link again.

[16:25] Miguel: On the pilot — suggested region is us-east-1. Any constraints for multi-region listings?

[16:33] Marina: Pilot in us-east-1 is easiest. For multi-region we recommend adding region-specific images and documenting regional endpoints. Keep pilot simple.

[16:50] Danielle: We'll aim to deliver the artifacts by 2026-09-21. Ibrahim will provide the SOC2 matrix by 9/20.

[17:05] Marina: Great. Last section: support and escalation. We'll capture a support contact and OLA for the pilot. Claire from Partner Ops will own the first line coordination.

[17:18] Claire: I'll set up a shared slack channel and a confluence space for artifacts and will invite the Solaris team.

[17:30] Priya: Awesome. Quick parking lot: pricing model details, metering agent options, and a deep-dive with infra (Ethan + Danielle) to validate helm chart. Let's lock the infra deep dive for next week.

[17:45] Marina: Noted — I'll send calendar invites. Anything else?

[17:50] Miguel: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.

[17:55] Marina: Thanks all. We'll recap in email and post the checklist and sample helm repo.

(Recording ends)
